title: Completed rational and common-stage coefficient units and unit equations
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], its rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], the common finite-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], their pullback and tensor operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the coherent coefficient-system calculus and canonical pullback/tensor comparisons [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. Define $\mathbf1_{E,W}^{\mathrm{int}}$ to be the actual derived inverse limit of the coherent coefficient-ring unit, with its constructible proof, and identify its reduction with that coherent unit by the reduction/limit counit. Define $\mathbf1_{E,W}$ by rational localization. Define $\mathbf1_{\Omega,W}$ to be the common-stage pair represented by $\mathbf1_{E_0,W}$ at the least finite coefficient field $E_0$. The integral left and right unitors are the unique lifts of the coherent unitors under the tensor and unit reduction comparisons; the rational unitors are their localizations. The rational coefficient-extension unit is the unique scalar-extension isomorphism satisfying both tensor-unit squares. Its composite with the stage-transition isomorphism identifies the common-stage unit with the rational unit at each larger stage. Define the common-stage unitors to be the unique common-stage classes whose representatives at every larger field are the tensor-stage comparison, the coefficient-unit comparison, and the corresponding rational unitor. Finally, for a morphism $f:X\to Y$, define its pullback unit-condition predicate (at integral, rational and common-stage levels) to mean that there is a unique isomorphism $\epsilon:Lf^*\mathbf1_Y\cong\mathbf1_X$ such that, for every $M$, the canonical pullback/tensor comparison followed by $\epsilon$ and the left unitor equals the pullback of the left unitor, and the analogous right-unit equation holds. This defines the predicate; it does not assert the predicate for every $f$.
